description:
FILED s451z, from the #702/#703 probes.  PRE-EXISTING (identical before and
after that work).

    my @a = `printf 'x\ny\n'`;   perl: 2 elements     PCL: 1
    my @b = qx{printf 'p\nq\n'}; perl: 2 elements     PCL: 1

perl's `readpipe` is wantarray-sensitive exactly like `readline`: in list
context the child's output is split on `$/` and each line KEEPS its
terminator.  `p-backtick` (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) returns the whole output as
one string in every context.

SEVERITY: silent wrong, and the value flows onward -- `for my $l (`cmd`)`
iterates once over the whole output, and `chomp(my @l = `cmd`)` leaves the
inner newlines.

FIX SHAPE (not designed): the sibling is `p-readline`, which already reads
`*wantarray*` and splits on `$/`; `p-backtick` should ask the same question
through the same splitter (rule 11) rather than growing its own.  Note the
`$/` rule is the same one, including `local $/ = undef` (one element) and
`local $/ = ""` (paragraph mode) -- probe both.

BAR: the two rows above, scalar context unchanged, `$/` set to undef / "" /
a custom string, output with no trailing newline, empty output (perl gives an
EMPTY list in list context and "" in scalar), and t/op/exec.t rows 7-13 which
already cover the scalar side.
subject: A command capture in LIST context returns ONE string -- perl splits it into lines (`my @a = `cmd`` gives 1 element, not 2)
